title: Driver compatibility checklist & vendor gap analysis (on-prem)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist + vendor gap analysis focused on GPU driver, CUDA and NCCL compatibility for on-prem Kubernetes clusters that host Redwood Private. Goal: reduce upgrade shock and provide clear terraform module knobs + smoke tests for rollouts. Intended readers: infra engineers, SREs supporting private customers, and solutions engineers preparing pre-install checklists.

Scope / assumptions:
- Target platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, RHEL 9 (customer-constrained), and a small set of validated OEM nodes (Dell PowerEdge, HPE ProLiant, Supermicro).
- GPUs: NVIDIA A10, A100 (40GB), and RTX A4500 in early customer labs. No AMD GPUs yet.
- K8s: v1.25 - v1.28 in active fleets; v1.29 considered experimental.
- Container runtimes: containerd (primary), dockerd (legacy customers).
- Kernel constraints: kernel ABI changes on RHEL HWE kernels are common failure mode.

High-level recommendations (TL;DR):
- Pin kernel+driver pairs in terraform module outputs for each node pool.
- Always run a lightweight smoke test after driver install: nvidia-smi, simple CUDA vector-add, NCCL ring-of-1 test inside a privileged pod and then inside user-runtime container.
- Add a "driver-compatibility" Terraform plan check that renders the resolved compatibility tuple (OS kernel, driver version, CUDA, NCCL, k8s CRDs) and flags risky combos.

Compatibility matrix (concise view) - keep this updated in Confluence canonical id CONFLUENCE-1234:
- Ubuntu 22.04 (kernel 5.15): NVIDIA driver 535.x -> CUDA 12.2 -> NCCL 2.17: supported for k8s 1.25-1.28 with containerd.
- Ubuntu 22.04 (kernel 5.19 HWE): driver 545.x -> CUDA 12.3 -> NCCL 2.20: supported but needs 545+ drivers compiled with same kernel headers.
- RHEL 9.2 (kernel 5.14 backport): driver 525.x -> CUDA 11.8 -> NCCL 2.14: conservative default.
- A100 40GB firmware required >= 52.4 for large model KV cache stability when using MIG.

Notes on mapping logic (why these things break):
- Drivers are kernel modules; mismatched kernel headers in the node image cause module build failures. For DKMS-enabled installs we need matching build-essential and correct gcc.
- CUDA toolkits used in user containers need ABI compatibility with host driver. If driver is older than toolkit-major-version (e.g., driver supports CUDA 12.x and container wants 13.0), runtime failures (unsatisfied library symbols) will occur.
- NCCL uses ibverbs/rdma and kernel ULP plugins on Mellanox NICs; IB stack mismatches cause silent hangs in cross-node allreduce.

Terraform module notes (practical knobs to add):
- node_pool_gpu_driver_version (string) -> explicitly set driver package to install (rpm/deb or URL).
- node_pool_force_reinstall (bool) -> used by upgrade job to force reinstall when kernel changed.
- gpu_vendor_firmware_url (string) -> optional firmware blob to stage and flash via vendor fwupd or nvidia-smi.
- node_pool_post_install_hook (script) -> path to a script that runs smoke tests (we use a containerized runner).
- driver_install_mode: [ "package", "dkms", "containerd-driver" ] -> to handle diverse customer environments.
- terraform plan hook: generate compatibility_report.json (simple text table) as a plan output.

Suggested terraform lifecycle for driver upgrades (manual + automated safe path):
1) Stage: run plan that outputs compatibility_report.json and human-readable notes.
2) Canary node pool: create a node pool with same instance type but 1-2 nodes, set node_pool_force_reinstall=true and driver_install_mode=dkms or package per customer.
3) Run smoke battery (below). Leave canary running 24-72h for perf/telemetry.
4) If canary passes, proceed rolling upgrade with maxUnavailable=1 and automated rollback on smoke failure.

Smoke battery (must be automated; container image: redwood/driver-smoke:v0.3):
- Privileged checks (host PID/ns): nvidia-smi -L, nvidia-smi topo -m, lsmod | grep nvidia, kernel log tail for nvidia errors.
- In-container CUDA: run vector-add (single-GPU) and small matrix-mul (multi-thread) to ensure cuBLAS/cuDNN entries load.
- NCCL: run ring test with --nranks=2 on same host and across nodes if networking is available (use NCCL_TESTS image). Patterns to watch: hangs during NCCL scalar ops (usually IB RDMA mismatch).
- MIG test (if A100): create 1 small MIG and run allocation test.
- Perf guardrails: verify p99 latency for a simple generation workload (local model microservice) doesn't regress >15%.

Failure modes and quick triage checklist:
- Module build fails during dkms: check kernel-headers version and gcc on host -> if mismatch, apply node_pool_force_reinstall after installing correct headers.
- nvidia-smi returns driver not loaded but device visible: check dmesg for TAINT or firmware missing; consider flashing firmware.
- Containers crash with /usr/local/cuda/lib64/* undefined symbols: driver too old vs container CUDA; either bump driver or rebuild containers with compatible toolkit.
- NCCL hangs (allreduce): verify ibv_devinfo, mlxconfig, and kernel mlx5_core version; if using SR-IOV or VF passthrough, ensure vf drivers are bound correctly.

Open questions / TODOs (work in progress):
- Should terraform module include an optional "driver-container" approach where the host runs a small shim that mounts driver libs into containers (experimental)? Pros/cons? (Priya to prototype)
- How to better surface firmware requirements for A100 MIG across customer fleet? Add firmware_version tag to terraform node_pool metadata?
- Add automatic rollback policy in TF that can mark nodepool unhealthy and increase pool size? Need design review with SRE.

Notes for solutions engineering (customer checklist to send before Private onboarding):
- Provide node OS image and exact kernel version (uname -r) for all node pools.
- Provide BIOS/firmware baseline and GPU firmware versions (nvidia-smi -q | grep -i firmware).
- Confirm network fabric (IB/ethernet) and whether RDMA is expected.
- Confirm container runtime; if dockerd, expect more fiddling for driver bind-mounts.

Example troubleshooting snippet (copy/paste for runbook):
- ssh to node -> sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver-installer -b -u cloud-init -xe | tail -n 200
- sudo dkms status
- sudo apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r) build-essential -y && sudo dpkg-reconfigure nvidia-driver
- docker run --gpus all --rm nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.2-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi && docker run --gpus all --rm redwood/driver-smoke:v0.3 /bin/sh -c "/opt/smoke/run-smoke-suite.sh"

Versioning proposal for record-keeping:
- Add node_pool.driver_manifest file in state bucket that records: driver_package, driver_version, cuda_supported_range, nccl_version, node_image_digest, kernel_version, firmware_version. Make the terraform module write this as an artifact on successful apply.

Appendix: quick compatibility heuristics
- If driver_major >= container_cuda_major -> usually ok. If driver_major < container_cuda_major -> fail.
- If kernel minor upgrade occurred since last deploy -> force rebuild of kernel module (use node_pool_force_reinstall).
- If NCCL hangs only on multi-node -> suspect IB stack, check MLX drivers + firmware.
